results.title: The function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the fraction field of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ indeterminates.

reading_title.source: The function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$

results.title: The roots $x_i$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$, $x_i$ is the $i$-th indeterminate of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, viewed as an element of its fraction field, the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

reading_title.source: The roots $x_i$

results.title: The coefficients of the general polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $0 \le i < n$, the coefficient $a_{i+1}$ is the $(i+1)$-st elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, as an element of the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

results.title: Coefficient field of the general polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be the field of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates and, for $1 \le k \le n$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$. The coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is the intermediate field of $\mathbb{C} \subseteq \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by $a_1, \dots, a_n$.

results.title: Coefficients in the coefficient field
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $0 \le i < n$, the coefficient $a_{i+1}$, the $(i+1)$-st elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, regarded as an element of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$.

results.title: The roots $x_i$ are pairwise distinct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the elements $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ are pairwise distinct: $x_i = x_j$ implies $i = j$.

reading_title.source: The roots $x_i$ are pairwise distinct

results.title: Algebraic independence of the elementary symmetric polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_1, \dots, e_n \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Injective algebra maps preserve algebraic independence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, let $f : A \to B$ be an injective $\mathbb{C}$-algebra homomorphism, and let $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $A$ that is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$. Then the family $(f(x_i))_{i \in \iota}$ is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: The coefficients are algebraically independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the coefficients $a_1, \dots, a_n$ of the general polynomial, the elementary symmetric functions of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

results.title: The roots are algebraically independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the roots $x_1, \dots, x_n$ are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

results.title: Polynomials in the roots
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every polynomial $p \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$, the image of $p$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ lies in the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra generated by the roots $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

results.title: Rational functions are algebraic over the polynomial subalgebra
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, every element of the field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates is algebraic over the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra generated by $x_1, \dots, x_n$: it is a ratio of two polynomials in $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

results.title: Transcendence degree of $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ has transcendence degree $n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, as a cardinal.

reading_title.source: Transcendence degree of $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$

results.title: Numeric transcendence degree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ that is a $\mathbb{C}$-algebra, the numeric transcendence degree of $F$ is its transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$ as a natural number when that degree is finite, and $0$ when it is infinite.

results.title: Elementary symmetric polynomials evaluated at the roots
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the image of the $k$-th elementary symmetric polynomial $e_k \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of the multiset of roots $\{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$, that is, the sum of the products $x_{i_1} \cdots x_{i_k}$ over all $i_1 < \dots < i_k$.

results.title: Coefficients indexed by degree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, for $1 \le k \le n$ let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, and let $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ be the coefficient field. For each natural number $k$, the element $c_k$ of $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is defined by $c_0 = 1$, $c_k = a_k$ for $1 \le k \le n$, and $c_k = 0$ for $k > n$.

results.title: General polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be the indeterminates of the rational function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, let $a_0 = 1$ and, for $1 \le k \le n$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$. The general polynomial of degree $n$ is the polynomial $\sum_{j=0}^{n} (-1)^j a_j X^{n-j} = X^n - a_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n a_n$ with coefficients in the coefficient…

results.title: Distinct linear factors are coprime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and distinct elements $a \ne b$ of the field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates, the polynomials $X - a$ and $X - b$ are coprime in $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)[X]$: there are polynomials $u$ and $v$ with $u (X - a) + v (X - b) = 1$.

results.title: The product of the linear factors $X - x_i$ is separable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n} (X - x_i)$ over the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is separable.

results.title: The roots generate the function field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the intermediate field of $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by the roots $x_1, \dots, x_n$ is the whole function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.

results.title: Each $x_i$ is a root of the general polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $E_n = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, and let $f_n = X^n - a_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n a_n$ be the general polynomial, with coefficients in $F_n = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n) \subseteq E_n$. Then $f_n(x_i) = 0$ in $E_n$ for every $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$.

results.title: The roots of the general polynomial generate the function field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $E_n = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, let $F_n = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n) \subseteq E_n$ be the coefficient field, and let $f_n = X^n - a_1 X^{n-1} + \cdots + (-1)^n a_n \in F_n[X]$ be the general polynomial. results.title: The trivial descent

results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the pair $(F, E)$ is a descent of the general polynomial extension, where $E = \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the field of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates and $F = \mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is the coefficient field, generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by the elementary symmetric functions $a_1, \dots, a_n$ of $x_1, \dots, x_n$.

results.summary: $\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q}$, also written $\mathbb{A}$, is the adele ring of $\mathbb{Q}$.

results.title: Height of a rational polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a multivariate polynomial with rational coefficients. Multiply the coefficients of $f$ by the least common multiple of their denominators and divide the resulting integers by their greatest common divisor; this gives the primitive integer coefficient vector $(a_m)_m$ of $f$, indexed by the monomials $m$ in the support of $f$. The height of $f$ is the Euclidean norm $\sqrt{\sum_m a_m^2}$ of this vector.…

results.title: Unimodular solutions of a polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative semirings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $f$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables indexed by a type $\sigma$. Then $f$ has a solution in $S$ if there is a vector $x \in S^\sigma$ whose components generate the unit ideal of $S$ and such that $f(x) = 0$, where $f$ is evaluated at $x$ through the algebra map $R \to S$.

results.title: Hypersurfaces of bounded height
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $A$, $\mathbb{V}_{d,n}(A)$ is the set of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces $V \in \mathbb{V}_{d,n}$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ whose height is at most $A$, where the height of $V$ is the height of the chosen nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ that represents $V$.

results.title: Everywhere locally soluble hypersurfaces
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: $\mathbb{V}^{\mathrm{loc}}_{d,n}$ is the set of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces $V \in \mathbb{V}_{d,n}$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ that are everywhere locally soluble, that is, with $V(\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q}) \ne \emptyset$: the chosen homogeneous polynomial representing $V$ has a solution in the adele ring $\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q}$, namely a zero given by $n + 1$ adeles that generate the unit ideal of $\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q}$.

results.title: Density of soluble Fano hypersurfaces
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 2$, $n \ge d$ and $(d, n) \ne (3, 3)$. Then the proportion $\rho_{d,n}(A)$ of degree-$d$ hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{P}^n$ of height at most $A$ that have a rational point tends to the local density $\rho^{\mathrm{loc}}_{d,n}$ as the real number $A$ tends to $\infty$.

results.title: Equiangular systems of unit vectors
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a real number $\alpha$ and a natural number $d$, an equiangular system with inner product $\pm\alpha$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of unit vectors in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space such that any two distinct vectors $x$ and $y$ in it satisfy $|\langle x, y \rangle| = \alpha$.

results.title: Maximum number of equiangular lines
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $\alpha$ and a natural number $d$, $N_\alpha(d)$ is the supremum, taken in $\mathbb{N}$, of the cardinalities of the equiangular systems of unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with inner product $\pm\alpha$. Here an infinite set counts as having cardinality $0$, and a set of natural numbers that is not bounded above has supremum $0$.

results.title: Spectral radius order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $\lambda$, the spectral radius order $k(\lambda) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least natural number $k$ such that some simple graph on $k$ vertices has an adjacency matrix with spectral radius $\max(\lambda, 0)$, and $k(\lambda) = \infty$ if there is no such graph.

results.title: Ramanujan's transformation of the alternating series of 1/(x^k - 1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real number $x$ with $|x| > 1$, we have $x^k - 1 \ne 0$ and $x^{k^2}(x^{2k} - 1) \ne 0$ for every integer $k \ge 1$, the series $\sum_{k \ge 1} (-1)^{k+1}/(x^k - 1)$ and $\sum_{k \ge 1} (-1)^{k+1}(x^{2k} + 1)/(x^{k^2}(x^{2k} - 1))$ are summable, and $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} (-1)^{k+1}/(x^k - 1) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} (-1)^{k+1}(x^{2k} + 1)/(x^{k^2}(x^{2k} - 1))$.

results.title: A finite identity for $\sum_k r^k/(1-ax^k)$ over a field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $a, r, x \in K$ and let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. Suppose that $1 - a x^k \ne 0$ and $1 - r x^{k-1} \ne 0$ for every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$. Then $\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{r^k}{1 - a x^k} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{(a r x^k)^k}{1 - a x^k} + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{a^{k-1} \left( (r x^{k-1})^k - (r x^{k-1})^{n+1} \right)}{1 - r x^{k-1}}$. For $n = 0$ all three sums are empty.

results.title: Rabin automaton
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Rabin automaton is a nondeterministic automaton together with a set of Rabin pairs $(E, F)$, each a pair of sets of states. A run is accepting when some pair is hit: the run visits $E$ infinitely often and $F$ only finitely often.

results.title: Membership in the language of a Rabin automaton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An infinite word $x$ is accepted by a Rabin automaton $r$ if and only if there is a run $s$ of $r$ on $x$ and a Rabin pair $(E, F)$ of $r$ such that $s$ visits $E$ infinitely often and visits $F$ only finitely often.

results.title: Rabin-to-Muller conversion preserves the language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the state space is finite, then a Rabin automaton $r$ accepts the same language as its Muller presentation: the Muller automaton with the same transitions and initial states as $r$ whose acceptance sets are the sets $S$ of states such that, for some Rabin pair $(E, F)$ of $r$, $S$ meets $E$ and is disjoint from $F$.

results.title: Streett automaton
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Streett automaton is a nondeterministic automaton together with a set of Streett pairs $(E, F)$, each a pair of sets of states. A run is accepting when every pair is respected: if the run visits $E$ infinitely often then it also visits $F$ infinitely often.

results.title: Membership in the language of a Streett automaton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An infinite word $x$ is accepted by a Streett automaton $r$ if and only if there is a run $s$ of $r$ on $x$ such that for every Streett pair $(E, F)$ of $r$, if $s$ visits $E$ infinitely often then $s$ visits $F$ infinitely often.

results.title: Streett-to-Muller conversion preserves the language

results.title: Rabin presentation of a parity automaton

results.title: Singleton bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite alphabet with $q$ letters, and let $n$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $1 \le d \le n$. If $C$ is a set of words of length $n$ over $\alpha$ in which any two distinct words are at Hamming distance at least $d$, then $C$ has at most $q^{n - d + 1}$ elements.

results.title: Closed Hamming ball
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite types $\iota$ and $F$, a word $x : \iota \to F$ and a natural number $e$, the closed Hamming ball of radius $e$ about $x$ is the finite set of all words $y : \iota \to F$ whose Hamming distance from $x$ is at most $e$.

results.title: Size of a Hamming ball
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For finite types $\iota$ and $F$, every word $x : \iota \to F$ and every natural number $e$, the closed Hamming ball of radius $e$ about $x$ has $\sum_{k=0}^{e} \binom{|\iota|}{k} (|F| - 1)^k$ elements.

results.title: Size of a Hamming ball of fixed-length words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $F$ be a finite alphabet with $q \ge 2$ letters. For every word $x \in F^n$ and every natural number $e$, the closed Hamming ball of radius $e$ about $x$ has $\sum_{k=0}^{e} \binom{n}{k} (q - 1)^k$ elements.
